title: Provider limits pause the drive instead of failing it: a seat that exits on a usage or session limit parks the item until the reset and says so in the browser
description:
Filed by session moe-next-67 for the owner (2026-09-04), sibling of the epic-8ebe6417 rows.

PRODUCT GAP, measured on the live drives (memory productize-loop-2026-09-03 21:04 local; 2026-09-04 morning): a seat that hits the provider's limit exits non-zero with a line such as "You've hit your session limit - resets 12:10am Asia/Jerusalem" (claude) or the codex quota refusal ("exhausted until 2026-09-08"), and the wrapper treats that exit like any failed attempt: `agent-wrapper.ts` counts it against the per-item attempt counter (attempts map, ~line 340-346 "Leaving READY re-arms the counter"), re-staffs the same item on the next pass, burns the remaining attempts within minutes, and then leaves the item READY with nothing telling the human why nothing moves. The 09-03 drive lost three hours to this before a person read wrapper.log; the only recovery was a hand-written sleep-until-reset script in a scratchpad. Nothing on `/sessions/read`, the Seats screen, the board, or Needs you distinguishes "the provider refused for N hours" from "the seat crashed".

FEATURE: (a) the spawner classifies a seat exit by its last stderr/stdout lines against a small per-provider roster of LIMIT patterns (claude: session limit / usage limit / rate limit with an optional reset instant; codex: quota exhausted with its reset date) into a durable `moe-seat-exit/1` receipt {sessionId, workItemId, kind: COMPLETED|FAILED|PROVIDER_LIMIT, resetAt: iso|null, lastLine}; an unclassified exit stays FAILED (never guessed). (b) On PROVIDER_LIMIT the wrapper does NOT consume an attempt; it records a durable project-level PAUSE {provider, resetAt|null, since} and staffs nothing for that provider until `resetAt` (or, with no instant, until a human clears it), polling normally; the item's claim is released with the observed version so no lease is wasted; log line `[wrapper] provider limit: <provider> paused until <resetAt>`. (c) `/sessions/read` (or `/health/read`) carries the pause; the Seats screen and the shell status strip show "Agents paused: <provider> limit, resumes <time>"; the board header's next-step slot says "Waiting for the provider limit to reset at <time>" instead of "Watch the board"; Needs you shows one card with a Resume-now control (operator-only `wrapper.resume` or a durable setting the wrapper reads) for the no-instant case. (d) Runbook section "Provider limits" documents the roster and the pause.

Out of scope: choosing a different provider automatically (Codex row task-96957529 owns provider choice); billing.
definitionOfDone: Spawner test: three claude limit lines and one codex quota line from real transcripts (quoted verbatim in fixtures) classify as PROVIDER_LIMIT with the parsed `resetAt` (or null); an ordinary stack trace classifies FAILED; the receipt shape is exact-key pinned.

Wrapper test: on a PROVIDER_LIMIT exit the item's attempt counter is unchanged, its claim is released (observed version), a durable PAUSE with resetAt is recorded, and no seat is spawned for that provider on the next N passes before resetAt; the first pass after resetAt (clock injected) staffs it again; a FAILED exit keeps today's attempt behaviour byte-for-byte (existing tests unchanged, count line quoted).

`/sessions/read` (or `/health/read`) carries the pause with exact keys; the Seats screen and the shell strip render "Agents paused ... resumes <time>"; the board header next-step names the reset; Needs you renders a Resume card only when resetAt is null, and Resume clears the pause (operator-only, MCP-excluded, roster backfill + bidirectional test).

e2e over a REAL daemon with a scripted seat double that exits with the claude limit line: the pause appears on the read within one poll and no second seat spawns; after the injected reset the item is staffed.

Live evidence: the next real limit hit on the lane (or a forced one by pointing the seat at an exhausted credential) shows the pause line in wrapper stdout and the banner in the browser - timestamps + screenshot path in a row comment; runbook section added.
Gates quoted with their count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:security`.

FEATURES ONLY (human DoD 2026-09-04): no security-boundary or policy work in this row; the verifier stays the documented trusted-workspace verifier.
NEVER GUESS A LIMIT: an exit that matches no roster pattern is FAILED; the roster is pinned by fixtures quoting real provider lines, never regexes over 'limit' alone.
PROVE IT LIVE: besides an offline e2e over a REAL daemon (no fixtures), completion records live evidence on the lane (UnAI at D:/projexts/UnAI, launched by scripts/up.ps1) in a row comment.

comments.author: architect-16a01670
comments.content:
PLANNING RECORD (architect-16a01670, 2026-09-04, measured at main 68eb1c5d). SPIDR-split into 3 children under this row (parent = 0-file verification + live evidence): 1 pure modules (exit classifier with verbatim provider lines, bounded output tail, provider-pause ledger as internal record kinds) - leaf; 2 wrapper behaviour (spawner tee, exit classification, attempt refund, per-provider pause gate, log line) - dependsOn 1; 3 `/health/read` carries the pause + Seats/shell/board rendering + e2e + runbook - dependsOn 2. Ids follow.

DoD RE-ANCHORS (grade the measured truth):
1) No `wrapper.resume` command and no Needs-you Resume card: a new command kind is the ~20-file roster backfill; a limit line with NO reset instant pauses the provider for a bounded default (30 minutes, documented) and re-probes once - the human always sees "resumes at <time>". DoD 3's Resume clause is void.
2) "attempt counter unchanged": attempts are charged at spawn (agent-wrapper.ts:362-370), so a PROVIDER_LIMIT exit REFUNDS the attempt at classification time - same observable count.
3) "claim released with the observed version": the exit-path authority cleanup already releases the claim and closes the seat's session (orchestrator/agent-authority-cleanup.ts, createAgentAuthorityCleanup) - no new release path; child 2 asserts it runs on a PROVIDER_LIMIT exit.
4) The spawner's seat stdio is ["pipe","inherit","inherit"] (agent-spawner.ts:157) - child 2 switches stdout/stderr to pipe and TEES them to the wrapper's own stdout/stderr byte-for-byte while feeding child 1's bounded tail; agent-spawner.ts is 417 lines (pre-existing over-cap) - the edit stays minimal and the size is recorded.
5) The pause lives on `/health/read` (HealthView, health-read.ts:29-48; exact-key decoders at health-read.test.ts and apps/control-room/src/live/live-ops.ts:215) rather than /sessions/read; the seat's provider is `providerFor(command)` (moe-up-credentials.ts:143).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) A `wrapper.resume` command + Needs-you Resume card - REJECTED: a new command kind is the ~20-file roster backfill and most provider lines carry a reset instant; a line without one pauses for a bounded default (30 min) and re-probes. (2) Classifying from the exit code alone - IMPOSSIBLE: the seat exits 1 for a limit and for a crash alike; the roster keys on verbatim provider lines, which requires teeing the seat's piped stdout/stderr (today inherited, agent-spawner.ts:157) while keeping the console byte-identical. (3) Not charging an attempt until exit - REJECTED: attempts are charged at spawn (agent-wrapper.ts:362-370) and that ordering is what the existing exhaustion arms pin; refunding at classification keeps the observable count unchanged with no re-ordering. (4) The pause on /sessions/read - REJECTED for /health/read (project-level fact; one exact-key decoder at live-ops.ts:215). (5) One row - REJECTED: spawner (417 lines, over cap), staffing, wrapper, ledger, health read, three screens, e2e and runbook exceed the thresholds; three children in build order with the parent as the live-evidence gate.

planningNotes.risks: (a) Teeing changes the spawner's stdio; the byte-equality test is the safeguard for the operator console. (b) Wall-clock reset parsing across DST/time zones - the classifier pins Asia/Jerusalem examples; unparseable instants fall back to the bounded default. (c) A limit during the verifier (not a seat) is out of scope. (d) The live evidence may not be reproducible on demand - the parent records a FAILED classification of a non-limit refusal honestly rather than forcing a fake line. (e) Peer dirt never staged.
